title: The Customer Interviews
description: You're Priya, six months after saving the chai stall. Now you want to grow — add ONE new menu item. Talk to FOUR very different customers before you decide. Listen for what they actually need under what they say.
learning_objectives: Practice asking open vs. closed questions in real conversations
Learn to paraphrase what a customer said before responding
Recognise the difference between stated complaints and underlying needs
Resist the founder reflex to pitch before you've listened
cultural_context: An Indian street-food entrepreneur learning that customers are the only reliable source of product truth — but only if you ask them right.
coaching_moment: Customers describe symptoms; founders find needs. The way you ask the question almost entirely determines the answer you'll get back.

scenario_series.synthesis_prompt: You've spoken to four customers. Now decide ONE thing to add to the menu. Pick the option that the most customers would ACTUALLY come back for, weighted by how well you listened.

synthesis_options.label: A corner bench (not a menu item — a place to linger)

scenario_series.best_answer_explanation: Samosa-chaat is the strongest single addition — it solves Rohit's hunger and Anjali's lingering ritual without pushing Lakshmi away (it's not sweetened) and doesn't conflict with Vikram's portable-energy need. Cold brew solves only Vikram. Oat-milk chai solves only Lakshmi. The corner bench is great but isn't a revenue-generating addition — it's a complement. The teaching beat: the best growth move serves multiple needs at once.

reflection_prompt: What's one thing you'll take from this game into a real-world situation this week?
